Page1.Title: Induction
Page1.Intro1: The letter said to report here. This is here — a Directorate terminal, humming quietly, waiting for a name it doesn't have yet.
Page1.Intro2: You're about to build the character you'll be playing. This takes most people twenty to thirty minutes. Nothing here is final — anything too complicated for a form gets finished properly once you're actually in the game, on your character's own sheet.
Page1.WhatToExpect: You'll choose who your character is — their ancestry, their background, their training — and answer a handful of real questions about who they are as a person, not just what they can do. If a question ever seems unclear, look for a small toggle that switches the form to plain, out-of-character language explaining exactly what's being asked. Every answer here feeds directly into the campaign; nothing is just flavour text. At the end, you'll have a working character and a token waiting for you at the table.
Page1.WhatYouNeed: Just a concept — a rough idea of who you want to play. Everything else, this form will ask you for, one step at a time.

Page2.Title: Ancestry
Page2.Intro: Your character's real ancestry — not the one they'll wear at the table. Every option here is real and mechanical; how it's disguised in play is entirely yours to decide later.
Page2.LoadFailedBody: That's this terminal's fault, not yours — nothing was lost. Use Back below, then Begin again; if it keeps happening, tell your GM.
Page2.HelpBody: Ancestry permanently sets six things on your sheet: two or three ability boosts (and sometimes one flaw), your base Hit Points, your Size, your Speed, and which languages you start with. It does not pick an ancestry feat — you'll choose one on your own character sheet once your token is on the table, the same way class feats work.
Page2.LockdownNote: Playing something other than Human, Elf, Dwarf, Gnome or Halfling is fully encouraged — it just means a few extra private questions later in the process. Those are between you and this screen; whether you ever tell anyone at the table is entirely your call, and there is no wrong answer.

Page3.Title: Background
Page3.Intro: Who your character was before the letter arrived. Every background is real and mechanical, same as ancestry — search or browse the full list below.
Page3.SkillsSeeDescription: This background's exact skill grant is a little unusual — see the description above for the real wording.
Page3.HelpBody: Background permanently sets three things on your sheet: two ability boosts, training in one or two skills (often including a Lore skill), and a skill feat. It does not pick the skill feat for you — you'll choose it on your own character sheet once your token is on the table, the same way ancestry and class feats work. A few backgrounds phrase their skill grant as a real choice ("Crafting or Piloting"); when that happens, the description above is the actual rule, not the summary rows below it.

Page4.Title: Class
Page4.Intro: The training your character actually received. Only six real specialisations exist — pick one below.
Page4.PlusMoreSkills: Plus {count} more skills of your choice — pick them on your own character sheet once your token is on the table.
Page4.HelpBody: Class permanently sets your key ability (the one every class feature and most of your best rolls key off), your Hit Points per level, starting Perception and saving-throw proficiencies, and your starting weapon/armor training. It does not pick your class features, feats or spells — those come next, on your own character sheet, once your token is on the table. Your Class DC starts Trained, same as every class at level 1.

Page5.Title: Attribute Boosts
Page5.Intro: Four more boosts, entirely your choice — on top of whatever your ancestry, background and class already set on their own pages. Each of the four below must go to a different ability.
Page5.HelpBody: This permanently raises one of the six numbers that drive almost every roll you make — the single most consequential page in this form. A free boost can land on an ability your ancestry, background or class already raised; it simply adds another +1 there. The four boosts below must each go to a different ability from each other, but not necessarily different from what's already been set elsewhere.

Page6.Title: Portrait
Page6.Intro: A photograph for your file — optional, but every character in this campaign uses the same frame, and it's a nice thing to have waiting for you at the table. Upload one below and adjust it to fit; Section Nine keeps standard imagery on hand for anyone who'd rather skip this.
Page6.InvalidFileType: That doesn't look like an image file — choose a photo (JPEG, PNG, WebP, etc.) instead.
Page6.FileTooLarge: That file is too large (over 20MB). Try a smaller photo.
Page6.HelpBody: There's no mechanical effect from your choice of photo, or from skipping it entirely. Every character portrait in this campaign is shown in the same tall frame, so keeping the crop close to the guide box just keeps your character looking consistent next to the rest of the cast once play begins.

Page7.Title: Finishing Details
Page7.Intro: The mechanical parts are done. This is the rest of who they are — a name, how they're addressed, and a few small things about them. Every box here has a row of suggestions you can click to fill it in fast, and every box is also just a box — write whatever you like instead, or as well.
Page7.BanalOptionalNote: None of this is required except your name — write as much or as little as you like.

Page8.Title: Personal Declaration
Page8.Intro: Eight real questions. Every answer becomes something the campaign actually uses — a connection, a side plot, a vulnerability, a running joke.
Page8.OptionalNote: Nothing on this page is required. Leave any or all of it blank and continue — you can always come back to this later.

Page9.Title: Review & Confirm
Page9.Intro: Everything below is what actually gets written down. Nothing is created until you confirm.
Page9.ConfirmNote: Class feats, spells, an ancestry/background feat, and any skills beyond what's listed above still need finishing on your own character sheet, once your token is on the table — same as every real character.
Page9.SuccessTitle: Done. You're in the system now.
Page9.SuccessBody: {actorName} exists, and your token is already waiting on the landing scene. Finish the rest — feats, spells, the last few skills — on your own character sheet.
